solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Freedom is, um… found in alcoholic drink

indicators.note: to be found in something is to sit inside it, so one piece is set within the other

blocks.note: er is the hesitation sound, like um
a libation is a drink, often a ceremonial pour of wine

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates mid-sentence, finding freedom at the bottom of a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis makes 'um' look like a speaker's pause, but it is a piece of wordplay; ER is the British spelling of that same hesitation noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberation is release from captivity or control, a straightforward synonym for the state of being free.

clue.text: Quality gag a turn getting Oscar prepared

blocks.note: taken as written
your go is your turn in a game
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
food that is done is ready, prepared

explanation.surface: A comedian's routine gets polished up before the Academy Awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quality gag a turn' reads like a review of a comedy act, and 'Oscar' suggests the film prize; here it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'that's a good one' praises a joke, so the phrase stands for a high-quality jest.

clue.text: Slogan that might grab you briefly?

indicators.note: made brief means cut short, so the final letter is lopped off

blocks.note: a mantrap is a snare set to catch trespassers

explanation.surface: An advertising catchphrase so punchy it seizes your attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'that might grab you' sounds like praise for a catchy slogan, but it describes a trap for people, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a phrase repeated constantly, much like a motto or watchword that people chant.

clue.text: Sorry Tory threesome making love to EU leaders

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so only the opening letter of each word counts
making one thing into another means swapping it, so one letter is turned into others

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
a trio is a group of three
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician apologises for a racy arrangement involving European leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: In the threesome, the love letter is replaced by the heads of 'to' and 'EU'. Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite describes someone feeling remorse for wrongdoing, a close synonym for being apologetic.

clue.text: Intolerant people can be bores outside of work

indicators.note: being outside something means wrapping around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: drill bits are tools that bore holes
a machine that goes is working

explanation.surface: A grumble that narrow-minded people are tedious company once the office day ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' wants to mean tiresome people, and 'outside of work' an evening out; instead the bores are tools that make holes, and they wrap around a verb meaning function.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigots are people who refuse to accept those with differing views, races or beliefs.

clue.text: Ultimately, flatulists with gas affected behaviour

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: air is a mixture of gases
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: In the end, people prone to wind have their behaviour altered by gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like a verb meaning changed by the gas; it is part of the definition, meaning pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs means adopting a pretentious, superior manner, so the plural noun matches pretentious conduct.

clue.text: Bunch of liars in government tell tales

indicators.note: a bunch is a group drawn from a larger whole, so a run of letters is taken from inside the words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word, the second word, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A complaint that a gang of dishonest politicians spin stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell tales' reads as lying, but here it means informing on others.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang, to sing is to inform to the police, the same as telling tales on accomplices.

clue.text: Desire to have union stirred up Paris, Idaho

indicators.note: something stirred up is mixed around, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A labour union agitating in the small town of Paris, Idaho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' looks like a trade union causing trouble; it is the physical union of lovers, part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodisia is sexual desire, named after Aphrodite, the Greek goddess of love.

clue.text: Ringer whose dirty pants might upset sprinter at the finish line?

definitions.text: Ringer whose dirty pants might upset

blocks.clueFragment: Ringer whose dirty pants might upset
blocks.note: first meaning: an obscene telephone caller who gasps down the line
second meaning: a runner gasping for air after the race

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is a verb, gasps, not underwear, and a 'ringer' is someone who phones you. The question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a nuisance caller who makes lewd panting noises and anyone gasping hard after exertion.

clue.text: Nice for one retired to cuddle small men

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold close in your arms, so one piece wraps around others

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
ret. is the abbreviation for retired

explanation.surface: A pensioner in a pleasant mood hugs some little fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' wants to be the adjective pleasant; capitalised, it is the French Riviera city. 'For one' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice is a famous holiday town on the Riviera, an example of a seaside resort.

clue.text: A tenor dwelling on run in off -Broadway theatre?

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the pieces follow one another
something put in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tenor in choral music
a house is a place to live
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A singer lives on a stage run at a small New York playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' suggests a show's season; it is the single letter used for a run in cricket scores. The question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: An arthouse venue shows experimental, non-commercial work, as off-Broadway stages do away from the mainstream.

clue.text: A lot of fences take up too much of a wood

indicators.note: to fence is to enclose land, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: many means a large number
to hog is to take more than your share
taken as written

explanation.surface: Garden fencing eats up a large part of the timber supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fences' reads as a noun, a supply of fencing panels, but it is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a reddish-brown tropical hardwood prized for furniture, an example of timber.

clue.text: Party currently holding power could be locked up

blocks.note: a party that is in is the one presently governing
a side is one party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: The governing party might well end up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the party first, but its letters go second: the party in government is the 'in' side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside is informal slang for serving time in prison, so it means jailed.

clue.text: One addict I sorted out shows devotion

indicators.note: sorting things out means rearranging them into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recovering addict takes pride in having got clean through sheer commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' sounds like getting clean, which suits the addict, but it is the signal to rearrange the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedication and devotion are close synonyms, both meaning wholehearted commitment to a cause or person.

clue.text: Naive ex-prince: “I need to change”

indicators.note: a change alters the arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gullible former royal confesses he must reform himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation reads as a royal's confession; the 'change' he speaks of is the instruction to rearrange all his letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inexperienced lacks worldly knowledge, so they are innocent or gullible, the sense of naive.

clue.text: God is on dope, according to a revisionist!

indicators.note: a revisionist rewrites the accepted version, so the order of letters is reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandalous historian claims the Almighty is a drug user.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a theological argument; 'God' is simply the definition, and the revisionist rewrites the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek deity of the sea, so he is an example of a god.

clue.text: It is a march in which rioting occurs!

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A protest is described as a demonstration that turned violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun opening the sentence; it is the definition, 'it' in the old sense of magnetic appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having 'it' is an idiom for possessing magnetic personal appeal, which is what charisma means.

clue.text: Spiritual knowledge boring? “No!” sister reveals

indicators.note: to reveal is to uncover what was concealed, so the letters were there inside the words all along

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A nun insists that religious enlightenment is anything but dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation breaks the words into a dialogue, but the letters run straight across it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis, from Greek for knowing, is mystical insight into divine truths, especially in early Christian sects.

clue.text: Jam on crustless rye is excessively dull

indicators.note: bread without its crust has lost its outer edge, so only the middle letter remains
in a down entry, on means sitting above, so the pieces stack in order

blocks.note: to jam something in is to stuff it
the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Jam spread on rye bread with the crusts cut off is a boring snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' and 'crustless rye' build a sandwich picture; jam is the verb meaning cram, and the crust is the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffy means stiffly formal and conventional, a strongly boring quality, so it suits tediously staid.

clue.text: Partnership coming from one-night stand, not date

indicators.note: not having something means it is excluded, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: a dalliance is a casual, brief affair
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A lasting relationship develops from a casual fling without any proper date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' suggests a romantic evening, fitting the fling; it is only its abbreviation, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or association formed for mutual benefit, matching partnership closely.

clue.text: Leaving cover, exposed privates will get pounded

indicators.note: in a down entry the cover is the top, and leaving it means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: to flash is to expose one's private parts indecently

explanation.surface: A streaker breaking cover is warned of a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privates' sounds like soldiers coming out of cover; it means private parts, and the cover is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain lashes a window when it beats down hard, so lashed means battered or struck repeatedly.

clue.text: Beer served by one’s husband makes you quite fat

indicators.note: being served by means having the next item brought alongside, so the pieces follow on

blocks.note: stout is a dark, heavy beer
one is I, and the apostrophe-s gives S
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A warning that beer poured by your other half will give you a paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' becomes a single numeral and a possessive S. Stout is a dark beer, Guinness being the best-known.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix '-ish' means somewhat, so stoutish describes someone moderately plump or a bit heavy.

clue.text: Third part of slogan found in Drink Coke!

blocks.note: surface padding that dresses the clue as an advertising jingle; it supplies no letters
first meaning: a bout of heavy drinking, a spree
second meaning: slang for a snort of cocaine

explanation.surface: An advertising jingle is quoted, its third word lurking in a soft-drink slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the soft-drink advert; 'Coke' is drug slang for cocaine, not the cola. The opening words frame the answer as a jingle sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is slang both for a drinking binge and for a sniff of cocaine.

clue.text: Religion is somewhat rubbish in total

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of it, so a portion of the words is taken

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismisses a faith as partly nonsense overall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' invites a verdict on the faith, but it only supplies letters; the answer runs across the gaps between three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous faith of Japan, centred on worship of kami spirits, an example of a religion.

clue.text: Green site scrooge with flu developed

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An environmental site was built up by a miser who caught a virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green site' suggests an eco-friendly location; the green is the putting surface at each hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf course is the ground where golf is played, made up of fairways and putting greens.

clue.text: Display behind flash old salesman’s back

indicators.note: the back of something is its tail end, so only the final letter counts

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, as in 'in a flash'
O is the abbreviation for old
the final letter of the word, ignoring the possessive

explanation.surface: A flasher bares all behind an old salesman's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Display behind' reads as showing something at the rear; it is the definition, to bare one's bottom. 'Flash' means an instant, not exposure.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon is to bare your buttocks at someone as a prank, literally showing your rear.
